title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The Engine Control Module (ECM) has detected a general malfunction in the Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) sensor circuit, which measures intake manifold pressure. This can affect fuel-air mixture calculations.
symptoms: Rough idle; Reduced engine power; Increased fuel consumption
actions: Check MAP sensor wiring; Verify sensor voltage output; Replace MAP sensor if faulty
location: On the intake manifold or airbox

title: MAP Sensor Circuit Low Input
problem: The ECM detects an abnormally low voltage signal from the MAP sensor, indicating a short to ground or an open circuit. This can lead to incorrect fuel delivery.
symptoms: Engine hesitation; Poor acceleration; Rich running condition
actions: Inspect wiring for shorts; Test sensor voltage at idle; Replace MAP sensor
location: On the intake manifold or airbox

title: MAP Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The ECM detects an abnormally high voltage signal from the MAP sensor, indicating a short to power or a faulty sensor. This can lead to incorrect fuel delivery.
symptoms: Engine stall; Lean running condition; Difficult starting
actions: Inspect wiring for shorts to power; Test sensor voltage under load; Replace MAP sensor
location: On the intake manifold or airbox

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECM has detected an inconsistent or incorrect signal from the Intake Air Temperature (IAT) sensor. This sensor provides air density information for fuel calculations.
symptoms: Poor fuel economy; Hard starting; Black smoke from exhaust
actions: Check IAT sensor wiring; Test sensor resistance; Clean or replace IAT sensor
location: In the airbox or intake tract

title: IAT Sensor Circuit Low Input
problem: The ECM detects a low voltage signal from the IAT sensor, often indicating a short circuit or an open circuit. This leads the ECM to assume cold intake air.
symptoms: Rich fuel mixture; Reduced engine performance; Increased emissions
actions: Inspect wiring for shorts; Test sensor resistance; Replace IAT sensor
location: In the airbox or intake tract

title: IAT Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The ECM detects a high voltage signal from the IAT sensor, suggesting an open circuit or faulty sensor. This leads the ECM to assume hot intake air.
symptoms: Lean fuel mixture; Engine knocking; Overheating
actions: Inspect wiring for opens; Test sensor resistance; Replace IAT sensor
location: In the airbox or intake tract

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECM has detected a general malfunction in the Engine Coolant Temperature (ECT) sensor circuit. This sensor is crucial for cold start enrichment and fan control.
symptoms: Difficult cold starting; Engine overheating; High idle RPM
actions: Check ECT sensor wiring; Test sensor resistance; Replace ECT sensor
location: On the cylinder head or water pump housing

title: ECT Sensor Circuit Low Input
problem: The ECM detects an abnormally low voltage signal from the ECT sensor, often indicating a short to ground or faulty sensor. This makes the ECM think the engine is very hot.
symptoms: Engine running rich; Poor fuel economy; Engine fan constantly on
actions: Inspect wiring for shorts; Test sensor voltage; Replace ECT sensor
location: On the cylinder head or water pump housing

title: ECT Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The ECM detects an abnormally high voltage signal from the ECT sensor, often indicating an open circuit or faulty sensor. This makes the ECM think the engine is very cold.
symptoms: Engine running lean; Overheating without fan; High idle RPM
actions: Inspect wiring for opens; Test sensor voltage; Replace ECT sensor
location: On the cylinder head or water pump housing

title: Throttle Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECM has detected a general malfunction in the Throttle Position (TP) sensor circuit. This sensor tells the ECM the throttle plate's angle.
symptoms: Erratic idle; Engine surging; Poor throttle response
actions: Check TP sensor wiring; Verify sensor voltage sweep; Adjust or replace TP sensor

title: TP Sensor Circuit Low Input
problem: The ECM detects an abnormally low voltage signal from the TP sensor, indicating a short to ground or an out-of-range adjustment. This often leads to reduced power.
symptoms: Lack of power; Engine hesitation; Stalling at idle
actions: Inspect wiring for shorts; Test sensor voltage at closed throttle; Adjust or replace TP sensor

title: TP Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The ECM detects an abnormally high voltage signal from the TP sensor, indicating a short to power or an out-of-range adjustment. This can cause over-fueling.
symptoms: High idle RPM; Unintended acceleration; Engine running rich
actions: Inspect wiring for shorts to power; Test sensor voltage at wide open throttle; Adjust or replace TP sensor

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
problem: The ECM has detected a general malfunction in the primary (upstream) Oxygen (O2) sensor circuit, which monitors exhaust gas oxygen content. This affects fuel trim.
symptoms: Poor fuel economy; Increased emissions; MIL illuminated
actions: Check O2 sensor wiring; Test sensor output voltage; Replace O2 sensor

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
problem: The primary O2 sensor circuit voltage remains consistently low, indicating a lean condition or a faulty sensor/circuit. This can cause the ECM to over-fuel.
symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust; Strong fuel smell; Reduced engine power
actions: Check for exhaust leaks; Inspect wiring; Replace O2 sensor

title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
problem: The primary O2 sensor circuit voltage remains consistently high, indicating a rich condition or a faulty sensor/circuit. This can cause the ECM to under-fuel.
symptoms: Engine hesitation; Poor acceleration; Increased engine temperature
actions: Check for fuel leaks/rich condition; Inspect wiring; Replace O2 sensor

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
problem: The ECM detects a malfunction in the heating element circuit of the primary O2 sensor. The heater brings the sensor to operating temperature quickly for accurate readings.
symptoms: Delayed closed loop operation; Increased emissions on cold start; Poor fuel economy
actions: Check heater circuit fuse; Inspect wiring; Replace O2 sensor

title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
problem: The ECM detects that the engine is running too lean (too much air, not enough fuel). This indicates a vacuum leak, fuel delivery issue, or exhaust leak.
symptoms: Engine misfires; Lack of power; Pinging or knocking sounds
actions: Check for vacuum leaks; Inspect fuel pressure; Clean fuel injectors

title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
problem: The ECM detects that the engine is running too rich (too much fuel, not enough air). This indicates a leaking injector, faulty fuel pressure regulator, or restricted air intake.
symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust; Strong fuel smell; Reduced fuel economy
actions: Check for leaking injectors; Test fuel pressure regulator; Inspect air filter

title: Injector Circuit Malfunction - Cylinder 1
problem: The ECM detects an open or short circuit in the electrical circuit for the fuel injector of cylinder 1, preventing proper fuel delivery.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power
actions: Check injector wiring harness; Test injector resistance; Replace fuel injector

title: Injector Circuit Malfunction - Cylinder 2
problem: The ECM detects an open or short circuit in the electrical circuit for the fuel injector of cylinder 2, preventing proper fuel delivery.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power
actions: Check injector wiring harness; Test injector resistance; Replace fuel injector

title: Injector Circuit Malfunction - Cylinder 3
problem: The ECM detects an open or short circuit in the electrical circuit for the fuel injector of cylinder 3, preventing proper fuel delivery.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power
actions: Check injector wiring harness; Test injector resistance; Replace fuel injector

title: Injector Circuit Malfunction - Cylinder 4
problem: The ECM detects an open or short circuit in the electrical circuit for the fuel injector of cylinder 4, preventing proper fuel delivery.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power
actions: Check injector wiring harness; Test injector resistance; Replace fuel injector

title: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects a general malfunction in the primary control circuit for the fuel pump. This can prevent the fuel pump from operating.
symptoms: Engine will not start; Engine stalls; Loss of fuel pressure
actions: Check fuel pump fuse; Inspect wiring to fuel pump relay; Test fuel pump relay

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor 'A' Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an erratic or absent signal from the Crankshaft Position (CKP) sensor. This sensor is vital for engine timing and RPM.
symptoms: Engine will not start; Engine stalls; Intermittent misfires
actions: Check CKP sensor wiring; Inspect sensor for damage; Replace CKP sensor

title: Camshaft Position Sensor 'A' Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an erratic or absent signal from the Camshaft Position (CMP) sensor. This sensor is used for valve timing and sequential fuel injection.
symptoms: Hard starting; Engine stalls; Reduced engine power
actions: Check CMP sensor wiring; Inspect sensor for damage; Replace CMP sensor

title: Ignition Coil 'A' Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 1)
problem: The ECM detects a malfunction in the primary or secondary circuit of the ignition coil for cylinder 1, leading to a loss of spark.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Reduced power
actions: Check spark plug; Inspect coil wiring; Replace ignition coil

title: Secondary Air Injection System Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an issue with the Secondary Air Injection (PAIR) system, which injects fresh air into the exhaust to burn unspent fuel and reduce emissions.
symptoms: Increased exhaust emissions; ""Check Engine"" light on; Possible backfiring
actions: Check PAIR valve vacuum lines; Test PAIR valve solenoid; Inspect air pump operation

title: EVAP Purge Control Valve Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an electrical malfunction in the Evaporative Emission Control System (EVAP) purge control valve circuit. This valve controls fuel vapor flow.
symptoms: Fuel smell; Reduced fuel economy; Hard starting after refueling
actions: Check EVAP purge valve wiring; Test purge valve solenoid; Replace purge valve
location: Near the fuel tank or airbox

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor 'A' Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an erratic or absent signal from the Vehicle Speed Sensor (VSS). This sensor provides road speed information for various engine and transmission functions.
symptoms: Inaccurate speedometer; Engine management issues; Cruise control malfunction
actions: Check VSS wiring; Inspect sensor for debris; Replace VSS
location: On the transmission output shaft or wheel

title: Idle Control System Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects a malfunction in the Idle Speed Control (ISC) system. This system regulates engine idle speed.
symptoms: Erratic idle; Stalling at idle; High idle RPM
actions: Clean ISC valve; Inspect wiring to ISC valve; Replace ISC valve

title: System Voltage Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an incorrect or unstable system voltage, indicating issues with the battery or charging system. This affects all electrical components.
symptoms: Dim lights; Engine struggles to start; Intermittent electrical faults
actions: Check battery voltage; Inspect alternator/stator output; Check rectifier/regulator
location: Battery: under seat; Stator: left engine cover; Regulator: usually rear or side of bike

title: Serial Communication Link Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects a problem with the serial communication link, which is used for data exchange between control modules or diagnostic tools.
symptoms: Loss of communication; Multiple warning lights; Engine may not start
actions: Check wiring harness for damage; Inspect ECM connectors; Professional diagnostic scan

title: Internal Control Module ROM Error
problem: The ECM detects an internal read-only memory (ROM) error, indicating a fault within the ECM's permanent data storage. This is a severe internal ECM failure.
symptoms: Engine will not start; Multiple systems offline; Intermittent engine operation
actions: Check ECM power and ground; Inspect ECM connectors; Replace ECM

title: Fuel Pump Control Circuit/Open
problem: The ECM detects an open circuit in the fuel pump control circuit, preventing power from reaching the fuel pump. Similar to P0230 but more specific to an open circuit.
symptoms: Engine will not start; Fuel pump does not prime; No fuel pressure
actions: Check fuel pump circuit fuse; Inspect wiring for breaks; Test fuel pump relay

title: Malfunction Indicator Lamp (MIL) Control Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects a malfunction in the circuit controlling the Malfunction Indicator Lamp (MIL), also known as the "Check Engine" light.
symptoms: MIL does not illuminate; MIL always on; No visual indication of faults
actions: Check MIL bulb/LED; Inspect wiring to MIL; Check ECM output to MIL

title: Intake Air Temperature (IAT) Sensor Error
problem: Suzuki's proprietary code indicating a fault with the Intake Air Temperature (IAT) sensor circuit, affecting air density readings.
symptoms: Poor fuel economy; Hard starting; Black smoke from exhaust
actions: Check IAT sensor wiring; Test sensor resistance; Clean or replace IAT sensor
location: In the airbox or intake tract

title: Barometric Pressure Sensor (BPS) Error
problem: Suzuki's proprietary code indicating a fault with the Barometric Pressure Sensor (BPS), which adjusts fuel mapping for altitude changes.
symptoms: Reduced power at altitude; Poor engine performance; ""Check Engine"" light on
actions: Check BPS wiring; Verify sensor output voltage; Replace BPS
location: Usually integrated into the ECM or near the airbox

title: Tip Over Sensor (TO) / Bank Angle Sensor (BAS) Error
problem: Suzuki's proprietary code indicating a fault with the Tip Over Sensor. This sensor cuts ignition if the bike leans too far to prevent damage in a fall.
symptoms: Engine will not start; Engine stalls when riding; ""Check Engine"" light on
actions: Check sensor mounting orientation; Inspect wiring; Replace tip over sensor
location: Under the seat or near the battery box

title: Secondary Throttle Valve Actuator (STVA) Malfunction
problem: Suzuki's proprietary code indicating a fault with the Secondary Throttle Valve Actuator, which controls secondary throttle plates for smooth power delivery.
symptoms: Rough throttle response; Poor acceleration; Engine surging
actions: Check STVA motor and gears; Inspect wiring; Replace STVA

title: Secondary Throttle Position Sensor (STPS) Error
problem: Suzuki's proprietary code indicating a fault with the Secondary Throttle Position Sensor, which monitors the position of the secondary throttle plates.
symptoms: Loss of power; Erratic engine performance; Engine warning light
actions: Check STPS wiring; Verify sensor voltage output; Replace STPS
location: On the secondary throttle body shaft

title: Gear Position Sensor (GPS) Error
problem: Suzuki's proprietary code indicating a fault with the Gear Position Sensor, which provides gear selection information to the ECM and dashboard.
symptoms: Incorrect gear displayed; Engine not starting in neutral; Reduced power in specific gears
actions: Check GPS wiring; Inspect sensor for damage; Replace GPS
location: On the left side of the engine case

title: Idle Speed Control (ISC) Valve Error
problem: Suzuki's proprietary code indicating a fault with the Idle Speed Control (ISC) valve circuit. Similar to P0505.
symptoms: Erratic idle; Stalling at idle; High idle RPM
actions: Clean ISC valve; Inspect wiring to ISC valve; Replace ISC valve

title: Fuel Pump Relay Circuit Error
problem: Suzuki's proprietary code indicating a fault in the fuel pump relay circuit, preventing the fuel pump from receiving power. Similar to P0230 or P0627.
symptoms: Engine will not start; Fuel pump does not prime; No fuel pressure
actions: Check fuel pump fuse; Inspect wiring to fuel pump relay; Test fuel pump relay

title: Ignition Switch Signal Error
problem: Suzuki's proprietary code indicating an issue with the ignition switch signal, often related to the immobilizer system or main power supply.
symptoms: Engine will not start; Key not recognized; Security light flashing
actions: Check ignition switch wiring; Inspect immobilizer antenna; Replace faulty components

title: Exhaust Control Valve (SET Valve) Error
problem: Suzuki's proprietary code for a fault in the Exhaust Control Valve (SET valve) system, found on some performance models to optimize exhaust back pressure.
symptoms: Reduced engine power; Loud exhaust noise; ""Check Engine"" light on
actions: Check SET valve cables; Inspect SET valve motor; Clear debris from valve

title: Throttle Position Sensor D Circuit Low
problem: The ECM detects a low voltage signal from the secondary (D) throttle position sensor, indicating a short or open circuit. This acts as a redundancy check.
symptoms: Engine power reduction (limp mode); Engine hesitation; Loss of throttle control
actions: Inspect wiring for shorts; Test sensor voltage; Replace TP sensor assembly

title: Throttle Position Sensor D Circuit High
problem: The ECM detects a high voltage signal from the secondary (D) throttle position sensor, indicating a short to power or open circuit. Essential for safety checks.
symptoms: Engine power reduction (limp mode); Unintended acceleration; Error in throttle input
actions: Inspect wiring for shorts to power; Test sensor voltage; Replace TP sensor assembly

title: ECM Malfunction
problem: This is a general Suzuki-specific P-code indicating an internal ECM malfunction not covered by other specific internal errors. Requires deep diagnostics or replacement.
symptoms: Engine fails to start; Intermittent complete system failure; Multiple unrelated DTCs
actions: Check ECM power and ground; Inspect ECM connectors for corrosion; Replace ECM

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
problem: The ECM detects a low voltage condition in the heater control circuit for the upstream oxygen sensor. The heater ensures efficient sensor operation.
symptoms: Delayed closed-loop operation; Increased emissions on cold start; Poor fuel economy
actions: Check wiring for shorts to ground; Test heater element resistance; Replace O2 sensor

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
problem: The ECM detects a high voltage condition in the heater control circuit for the upstream oxygen sensor. This can indicate a short to battery voltage or an open circuit.
symptoms: Delayed closed-loop operation; Increased emissions on cold start; Fuse for O2 heater may be blown
actions: Check wiring for shorts to power; Test heater element resistance; Replace O2 sensor

title: Fuel Level Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an inconsistent or incorrect signal from the fuel level sensor, affecting the fuel gauge reading.
symptoms: Inaccurate fuel gauge; Fuel light stays on/off; Uncertainty about fuel quantity
actions: Check fuel level sensor wiring; Test sensor resistance; Replace fuel level sensor
